claims.claim: The mesh wire frame is a fixed 6-byte prefix carrying EXACTLY four decoded fields plus an opaque tail: dest (u16 LE, offset 0), src (u16 LE, offset 2), hopLimit (u8, offset 4), flags (u8, offset 5), inner (bytes 6..). TryDecode emits precisely these five outs; there is no other field. PrefixSize=6.

claims.claim: Of those four fields a forwarder consults only THREE: flags (bit 0x01 test, control-vs-data demux), dest (== self ? deliver : lookup next hop), and hop (<=1 ? drop). src is NOT consulted for any forwarding decision - it is only copied verbatim into the re-encoded forward and passed to the local delivery callback as the origin tag.

claims.claim: An originator therefore CANNOT express an intended PATH - only a destination and a hop budget. SendAsync's entire signature is (dest, payload, hopLimit, ct); the frame has no route vector, no waypoint list, no via field, and MeshRelayRoute.Decide re-derives the next hop purely from the local router's table, ignoring any originator preference. claims.claim: 7 of the 8 flag bits are carried end-to-end but never consulted: only bit 0 (FlagControl 0x01) is tested, and the forward re-encode preserves the whole flags byte unchanged. An originator can set bits 1-7 and every relay will propagate them to the destination unread and unauthenticated - a carried-but-unconsulted field (a covert channel), NOT a steering lever.

claims.claim: THE ATTACK SURFACE the cost bound does NOT cover: advert.Cost is a raw remote-supplied uint and IS the metric. Ingest computes rawCost = advert.Cost + linkCost and only bounds it from ABOVE (>= MaxCost 16 => Infinity). Nothing bounds it from BELOW: a neighbour may advertise Cost=0 for EVERY dest, yielding candidate == linkCost (1 by default) - the cheapest possible non-self route - and so elect itself next hop for the whole mesh (a black hole). The 016 codex-review fix cited at :96-97 defends only the wrap/overflow direction.

claims.claim: M-36 counterexample CONSTRUCTED (by reading, NOT executed at the pin): the seq ceiling is unrecoverable because NO node ever increments a seq. _selfSeq is initialised to 2 at declaration and read ONLY in the constructor - it is never incremented anywhere in the file. SetLinkState's poison deliberately KEEPS the seq (:170-173). Therefore after a hostile Seq=ulong.MaxValue/Cost=0 advert for dest X, every legitimate advert for X (seq 1 or 2) is rejected as stale forever; when the hostile link then drops, A's entry for X is poisoned at seq=MaxValue and no legitimate reroute can ever out-rank it => X permanently unreachable at A. Only a DIRECT link to X re-seeds it (AddNeighborNoLock at :185-192).

claims.claim: NOTHING compels a node to contribute route knowledge, and a non-contributor IS detectable but ONLY when a clock is injected: DistanceVectorRouter.Tick ages a dest out when now - LastRefreshTick > expiryTicks (default 30) and poisons it. claims.claim: There is NO delivery/receipt concept back to the originator.
